By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by section 301 of title 3 of the United 
States Code (65 Stat. 713), and as Pres­
ident of the United States, it is ordered 
th at the Secretary of State be, and he 
is hereby, designated and empowered 
to exercise, without the approval, ratifi­
cation, or other action of the President, 
so much of the authority vested in the 
President by the first section of the Joint 
Resolution of March 4, 1948, entitled 
“Joint Resolution providing for mem­
bership and participation by the United 
States in the Caribbean Commission and 
authorizing an appropriation therefor” 
(62 Stat. 66; 22 U. S. C. 280h) as con­
sists of authority to appoint alternate 
United States Commissioners to the Car­
ibbean Commission.

WHEREAS since the earliest days of 
our history American mothers have in­
spired our most exalted national ideals 
through their teachings and by example 
in their daily lives; and 
WHEREAS it has become our felici­
tous custom to set aside one day each 
year for commemorating motherhood 
and for showing our reverence and love 
for ali the mothers of the land; and 
WHEREAS in recognition of the fit­
ness of such commemoration, the Con­
gress, by a joint resolution approved 
May 8, 1914 (38 Stat. 770), has desig­
nated the second Sunday in May of each 
year as Mother’ s Day and has requested 
the President to issue a proclamation 
calling for the observance of that day: 
NOW, THEREFORE, I, DWIGHT D. 
EISENHOWER, President of the United 
States of America, do hereby request 
that Sunday, May 8, 1955, be celebrated 
as Mother’ s Day; and I  direct the appro­
priate officials of the Government to ar­
range for the display of the flag on all 
Government buildings on that day.
I also call upon the people of the Na­
tion to give public and private expres­
sion to the esteem in which our country 
holds its mothers, through the display of 
the flag at their homes and other suit­
able places, through prayers at their 
places of worship, and through appro­
priate manifestations of respect and 
devotion.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I  have 
hereunto set my hand and caused the 
Seal of the United States of America 
to be affixed.
DONE at the City of Washington this 
fifth day of May in the year of our Lord

TERM:EO:10609:045f398164ff8630@48015a572.text:
Tijdens
deze Zitting werd de volgende resolutie aangenomen:
"The Caribbean Council, at its Fifth Meeting taking into consider-
ation the implications of the decision of three Members of the
Caribbean Organization to withdraw, and the financial consequence
thereof:
Decides that the operations of the Central Secretariat shall be
terminated not later than December 31, 1965;
Requests that the Parties Signatory to the Agreement Establishing
the Caribbean Organization take such steps as are necessary to termi-
nate the Agreement on December 31, 1965, or as soon thereafter
as possible;
Recommends that a Working Group comprising all Members,
including the withdrawing Members, the Special Observers, and all
other interested democratic countries in the area, convene at the
earliest possible date to develop a formula or a series of formulae
to permit and provide for regional cooperation in the social, eco-
nomic, educational, and cultural fields;
Recommends further that before April 15, 1965, a meeting of
the above-mentioned governments be convened at the highest possible
level to decide the form and nature of regional cooperation.".

"The Caribbean Council,
Considering that the Government of Jamaica had already com-
municated to the Secretary-General its interest in considering the

Takes note of the statement by the United Kingdom Observer
